correctness.rationale: Every traceless \(2\times2\) matrix has square \((a^2+bc)I\), and its commutators give the three-by-three coordinate minors. Primitive nilpotent residue charts are smooth of relative dimension \(r+1\) and have \(q^{r+1}\) lifts per additional truncation degree. All-zero-residue jets reduce to the same equations at length \(m-2\), with exactly \(q^{3r}\) free highest coefficients. The exhaustive recurrence has verified initial values and solves to the claimed rational series. The nonzero-residue jet open set is irreducible; the closed origin fiber is \(\mathbb A^{3r}\) times the lower-length jet scheme. For \(r\ge3\), the dimension gap \(r-2>0\) proves the component ladder inductively. Complete small-case enumeration, extension-field computation and Jacobian-rank checks corroborate rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: The simultaneous square-zero commutator equations define a canonical higher nilpotent commuting variety related to singularity theory. An all-length rational point-count series for every odd finite field and arbitrary tuple length, and a complete rank-independent component ladder demonstrating a sharp transition at r=3, are substantive global structural invariants rather than an arbitrary finite numerical instance. They distinguish smooth primitive lifting from singular-origin arcs and connect nilpotent commuting geometry to arithmetic jet growth.
